newsitem.title: UK: Capital sees growth in restaurant sector.
newsitem.headline: Capital sees growth in restaurant sector.

text.p: Capital Radio Plc said on Monday its planned acquisition of My Kinda Town Plc would create a unique entertainment brand aimed at young adults with disposable cash.
Speaking at a news conference, Capital executives denied that the 51 million stg move into the themed restaurant market was reckless.

"No-one has combined restaurants and radio stations...We think that this is a great idea and we want to get in quickly," said managing director Richard Eyre. He said the acquisiition should be earnings enhancing from the first full year.
Leading British commercial radio company Capital earlier announced a recommended 190p per share offer valuing My Kinda Town at some 51 million stg.
The two already have a joint venture to run the "Capital Radio Cafe" which will open later this month in London.
My Kinda Town has 54 outlets in 16 countries. Capital said that the "radio cafe" concept could be developed further.

It also said it planned to exploit cross-promotional opportunities between radio stations and the restaurants and use its skills at putting on entertainment events to draw more customers into the venues.
The restaurant brands include The Chicago Pizza Pie Factory, The Chicago Rib Shack and Henry J Bean's bar and grill.
Capital stressed that radio remained its core business and said it believed the market would continue to grow at a rate of in excess of 4.5 percent.
It said that new media ownership rules left it considerable scope for acquisitions in the UK to add to its stations in Birmingham, London and the southern counties.
It identified the Internet as the fastest growing advertising medium of the future and pinpointed this as the focus for its cross-media expansion, having recently set up its own web site.
It said there were only minimal synergies between radio and other conventional media such as newspapers and television and ruled out investment in these.
It also announced plans to launch a record label as part of a joint venture with Telstar Records and Wildlife Management.
The plan is to sign up two artists in year one, with an initial investment of around 250,000 stg.
